subject: History
description: Last Delhi Sultanate dynasty, Bahlul, Sikandar, Ibrahim, Panipat 1526, art and architecture

questions.stem: The Lodi Dynasty, the last ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, was founded in 1451 by:

options.option_text: Bahlul Lodi (an Afghan noble who deposed the last Sayyid sultan)

questions.explanation: Lodi Dynasty (1451-1526) — Afghan in origin (most Sultanate dynasties were Turkic). Founder Bahlul Lodi (r. 1451-89) — was governor of Sirhind under the Sayyid sultans; deposed Alam Shah, the last Sayyid sultan, on 19 Apr 1451. Three rulers: Bahlul, Sikandar (1489-1517), Ibrahim (1517-26). The Lodis were the FIRST Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. The dynasty ended with Ibrahim's defeat and death at the First Battle of Panipat (21 Apr 1526) by Babur — marking the start of the Mughal Empire.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Sikandar Lodi (r. 1489-1517), the most capable Lodi ruler, founded which present-day major city as his new capital?
questions.explanation: Sikandar Lodi — founded the city of Agra in 1504 on the right bank of the Yamuna; shifted capital from Delhi to Agra in 1506. Reasons: better central location to control Doab + Bayana, Gwalior, central India; relief from Delhi's overcrowded politics. Agra later flourished as the Mughal capital (Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan). Sikandar's other achievements: stable administration; introduced 'Gaz-i-Sikandari' (Sikandari yard, ~30 inches, used as a measure for land); patronised Persian + Hindi literature; commissioned 'Lahjat-i-Sikandari' on music. Was an iconoclast — destroyed many Hindu temples in Mathura, Utgir, Jwalamukhi.

questions.stem: The First Battle of Panipat (21 April 1526) was fought between:
questions.explanation: First Battle of Panipat — 21 April 1526; Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi. Babur was invited to invade by Daulat Khan Lodi (governor of Punjab) and Alam Khan (Ibrahim's uncle), both at odds with Ibrahim. Babur's force ~12,000-15,000 vs Ibrahim's ~100,000 + 1,000 elephants. Babur won decisively due to (1) tulughma — flanking-attack tactic; (2) artillery — first major use of gunpowder cannons in India (master-gunner Ustad Ali); (3) breast-defence with carts (araba). Ibrahim was killed in battle — only Delhi Sultan to die in battle. Babur founded the Mughal Empire (1526-1857). Battle of Khanwa (1527) — Babur vs Rana Sanga. Second Panipat (1556) — Akbar vs Hemu. Third Panipat (1761) — Marathas vs Ahmad Shah Abdali.

questions.stem: The 'Lodi Gardens' in central Delhi contain the tombs of Lodi-era rulers including the:

options.option_text: Tombs of Sikandar Lodi and Mohammad Shah (Sayyid)
Tomb of Ibrahim Lodi (he is buried at Panipat)

questions.explanation: Lodi Gardens (90-acre park, central Delhi, near Khan Market) — contains: (1) Tomb of Mohammad Shah (Sayyid sultan, 1444); (2) Tomb of Sikandar Lodi (1517); (3) Bara Gumbad (1490, prob a gateway to a missing mosque); (4) Sheesh Gumbad (Sikandar Lodi era). Ibrahim Lodi's tomb is at PANIPAT (where he died) — a simple unadorned structure. Iltutmish's tomb — in Qutb complex (Mehrauli), early 13th c. Akbar's tomb — Sikandra (Agra). Lodi tombs marked transition to octagonal + double-domed pattern that culminated in Humayun's Tomb and the Taj Mahal — early experiments with the Indo-Islamic mausoleum form.

questions.stem: Daulat Khan Lodi, the governor of Punjab whose invitation indirectly brought Babur into India, did so because:

options.option_text: He wanted Babur to be his son-in-law
He resented Ibrahim Lodi's centralising and harsh policies toward the Afghan nobles
Babur was the rightful heir to Delhi

questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi (r. 1517-26) — tried to centralise authority and humiliated several senior Afghan nobles (a key error since Lodi rule rested on the consent of the Afghan tribal nobility). Daulat Khan Lodi (governor of Punjab) and Alam Khan (Ibrahim's own uncle, who claimed the throne) sent emissaries to Babur in Kabul, asking him to invade and depose Ibrahim. Babur — already familiar with Punjab from previous raids (1519-24) — accepted. By the time Babur reached Delhi, Daulat Khan had reconsidered and tried to oppose Babur — but his army melted away. The invitation–defection pattern was a classic Lodi-era weakness; Sher Shah Suri later exploited similar tribal disaffection against the Mughals.

questions.stem: Sikandar Lodi was a notable patron of the Persian translation of the great Sanskrit medical / Ayurvedic treatise. The translated Sanskrit work was:

options.option_text: Ayurveda treatises (a work titled Tibb-i-Sikandari or Ma'din-ush-shifa-i-Sikandar Shahi was compiled in his time)

questions.explanation: Tibb-i-Sikandar Shahi / Ma'din-ush-shifa-i-Sikandar Shahi — a Persian compilation of Indian medicine commissioned during Sikandar Lodi's reign (compiled by Miyan Bhuwa, son of his minister). Ayurvedic remedies were translated from Sanskrit. Sikandar also patronised music — 'Lahjat-i-Sikandari' (treatise on music). Sanskrit-to-Persian translation traditions later flourished under the Mughals — Akbar's Razmnama (Mahabharata) and Ramayana translations; Dara Shukoh's translation of Upanishads (Sirr-i-Akbar, 1657). Lodi-era cultural sponsorship was modest but transitional, paving the way for the Mughal florescence.

questions.stem: Bahlul Lodi spent most of his reign (1451-89) consolidating control over which troublesome eastern principality, finally succeeding in 1483?
questions.explanation: Bahlul Lodi spent most of his reign in long campaigns against the Sharqi Sultanate of Jaunpur (founded 1394 after Timur's invasion fragmented the Tughlaq empire; capital Jaunpur in eastern UP; also called the 'Shiraz of the East' for cultural patronage — Atala Masjid, Lal Darwaza Masjid, Jami Masjid). Bahlul finally annexed Jaunpur in 1483; the Sharqi sultans took refuge in Bihar. This expansion brought the Doab + eastern UP firmly under Lodi rule. Bengal Sultanate (Iliyas Shahi, Hussain Shahi) — independent throughout, conquered by Mughals later. Vijayanagara — south India (1336-1646). Bahmani Sultanate — Deccan (1347-1527, fragmented into 5 sub-sultanates including Ahmednagar, Bijapur, Golconda).
